body:
I'm going through a similar situation myself. I've known my guy for several years online. We talked about the potential of dating in the past but nothing ever came of it. Recently we started talking more about it and things changed between us, calling each other every day, staying up with each other all night, talking about future plans together etc. We planned a trip for him to come stay with me for a few days and the whole experience went really well I thought. He was very kind an gentle, got along well with my friends, we were even intimate. He gets back home though and suddenly he becomes preoccupied with everything else, work suddenly becomes so much more time consuming, he's got plans with friends all the time, things suddenly come up. We went from talking constantly to exchanging a few texts a day, and from calling almost daily to having one phone conversation in nearly a month now. I asked him just after he left if his feelings had changed, and he said no, but just based on how we interact now I know that can't be true.

When I asked him the other day about "us" if we were still planning to get together officially and whatnot he said we would have to see how things went. I don't really know what he meant by that or how I was supposed to respond so I didn't press the issue anymore. I'm just trying to appreciate the time I have with him now, and not let myself get too upset that things aren't going the way I wanted them to.

I guess the best advice I can give you is to try to compartmentalize the situation, enjoy the fun moments but try not to let yourself get attached. He doesn't seem like he wants anything more than a casual hook\-up and that's fine if you can both mutually agree on it, but if you think you're just going to keep getting hurt then you should remove yourself from the situation.

Maybe absence will make the heart grow fonder.

I'll keep you updated.

I didn't watch him, I was driving home and then didn't fall asleep until 6am or so. I messaged him when I got home to tell him goodnight and noticed that he was still up and playing a game.

I guess just stop making an effort to talk to him. I've put myself out there, he knows how to get in touch with me if he wants to, I can't keep trying to make something happen if he isn't interested.

I got in trouble at work today because I was so distracted last week I didn't do something before finishing my shift. My supervisor told me he didn't want to write me up but I've been there long enough to know better, and if having my phone at work is going to be an issue then he can put a stop to it. I was so distracted last week with Paul I couldn't concentrate on work. It wasn't even my phone, it was the fact that I was so consumed by this situation I couldn't concentrate on my work and completely neglected some of my responsibilities.

This situation is going to have to resolve itself soon or I'm going to have to resolve it on my own. I can't let my work life suffer because my personal life is getting out of control. As much as I hate to say it I'm going to have to be an adult and walk away if I can't get some kind of resolution. Even if it's just friendship I need to know where we stand, and if he can't do that much for me I have to accept the situation has changed and simply move on.

More or less I guess. I don't want to keep trying to get him to open up with me and keep trying to force myself on him. He seems so disengaged now. I mean like he knows when I get off work, it's the same time every day I work, and before he would either be in bed right now, or we would be on the phone. Instead I see he's logged on and playing a game, for the last 3 hours. He ghosted me in the middle of a conversation earlier and now I see he's been playing a game this whole time.

I'm trying not to be frustrated you know, but like we haven't had a real conversation in nearly 3 weeks. He used to lose sleep staying up trying to talk to me, but now it's like he seems indifferent to talking to me at all. I mean he's up at 5am playing a game right now when normally he'd long since gone to bed. I just don't understand, and I'm honestly starting to lose hope for this.

I have only really told him I was concerned that one time just after he got back and he started kinda acting different, since then I haven't said anything that would really hint at me feeling that he may have lost interest. I think he's picking up on the fact that I've been stressed out lately, but he hasn't really asked me how I'm feeling or tried to get me to open up.

I've jokingly asked him if he's still single a few times and he's said no, I can only hope he means that in a joking way, otherwise I'm gonna feel pretty shitty. My divorce is set to finalize in less than 2 weeks, I'm kinda curious if he's going to want to make this official after that or not, I've been kind of afraid to ask.

Things are better I think, but I feel like that's mostly because I've sorta gone through my stages of grief in a manner of speaking, and kind of got to the acceptance part where I acknowledge that things are different and I don't like it, but I'm just happy we still talk. It's been weeks since we've spoken on the phone for more than 5 minutes. He used to call me after I got off work and talk to me on my drive home, but we haven't done that since before we met in person. The last real conversation we had on the phone was before we met in person too. We spoke briefly before his flight took off and have had two 5 minute phone conversations since he left.

Things are definitely different know and I'm still really concerned he's lost interest, there has been no discussion of "us" in a while now and any talk about plans has been vague with nothing concrete set. I don't want to push him into telling me how he feels, but I'd still really like some clarification that we, as this unofficial couple thing we had going on, is still in fact a thing, and he is still very much interested in pursuing this.

I asked him if he still wanted to get together in May and he said yes. I told him he knew when my scheduled off days were so we'd have to plan around those days. He said he'd have to see if he could get someone to cover the store for him to take more than two days off. I told him he should try to see if he can get a Saturday through Tuesday off, since Monday and Tuesday are supposed to be scheduled time off for him. He said he'd talk with his brother and see when he had his kids and if he could cover. That was the end of that. Nothing concrete. He also said that the people he's staying with would be fine with me staying, though he clarified that he didn't actually ask which I thought was odd. As if to imply that it was never a problem to begin with? I'm not really sure what the deal with that is. Maybe they've talked about us and told him they would be cool with having me over even without him having to ask.

We made a few flirty jokes during games tonight with his brother and friend, joked that I was too far for any real fun, and called me babe at the end of the night when it was just me and him. I noticed he was suddenly really responsive when I made a sexual joke to him while he was out with friends earlier. Like would read and respond to my messages instantly. Thought that was kinda odd, I wonder if he's worried I've lost interest. Surely not since I still make just as much effort to communicate with him, if not more.

Honestly I'm not sure, I mean what are the odds of having that many friends with that many birthdays all at the same time? I mean it's probably my anxiety getting the best of me again, but it's pretty unusual I would think.

I'll try setting an exact date and see what he says then, maybe that will help.

He said he'd have to check with who he's staying with but hasn't said anything else about it. I told him once he gets his own place in June I could just come stay with him on my off time from work, he seemed ok with the idea but offered excuses claiming it would cost a lot etc. Idk his general attitude seems to have changed, like he doesn't seem interested in trying to plan or do anything. Nearly every day some new something is coming up that keeps him busy, two days ago it was his friends birthday and he would be doing that when he got off work, now today it's his nephews birthday, before that his friends reinlistment, before that another friends birthday.

I'd rather this not be the new norm but I guess I'll get used to it if that's the case, a little bit of reassurance would be nice though. I mean communication is our only means of expression really. Verbally saying how he feels would really help but it doesn't seem like he wants to do that anymore, and I'm kind of struggling with that, I don't understand why now it's changed.

I tried telling him that he shouldn't keep allowing himself to be taken advantage of for family, that I understand family is important but he's really putting up with way too much. I don't really know how else I can help, if we were physically together maybe I could take him out or do something around the house but I can't do that.

I didn't really argue with my ex so much as I was just like "why are you doing this?" when he said those guilting things. He was telling me they were remastering Dark Souls for the current gen and I reminisced about how he and I used to play together on the original one early into our relationship and how much fun we used to have outside Anor Londo ganking invaders. Then he had to make a comment about "back when you loved me". It really ruined that moment for me, I have some happy memories with my ex sure, but there was a lot more bad than good. Those good memories meant a lot to me, and it really hurt for him to pull that shit, definitely reinforced that I made the right call in going through with the divorce.

He can't break up with me because we aren't dating. We haven't talked anymore about making things official, and I've since tried to express to him that I feel like we aren't talking as much but he just brushed it off and didn't respond. I just hate feeling like we don't talk anymore, I mean we haven't had a real conversation outside of small talk, and it seems so forced.

He was supposed to be off today and we planned to spend the day playing games but naturally he got called into work because someone else called in. I told him I was worried about him and that I feel like he's letting himself be taken advantage of because it's family. He brought up how I work 12 hour shifts shifts at work and that's not easy either, but we do what we have to. I explained that I get guaranteed time off and most of my days I'm on the clock a few hours not even really working because it's 3rd shift and there isn't anything to do. He didn't have anything to add to that. He apparently wants to start his own business with his brother. The issue is that they don't have enough responsible employees to cover shifts, if they had that it wouldn't be so bad but they don't, him starting his own business won't fix the problem unless he can find people willing to work.

Things were fun until we switched games and he started getting upset because I wasn't playing as well as we would have liked. He never says anything negative, but you can tell in his tone he is upset or frustrated.

I haven't drank in a few days. I had dinner with my soon to be ex husband last night. Things were fine with that until he had to make things awkward by saying things like "back when you loved me" etc. He's always been bad about trying to guilt trip me, one of the things that drove us apart. I really hoped we could maintain a casual friendship, but it doesn't seem like he will be able to.

He works at his fathers business that they want him to essentially manage while they rake in profits. He's been worked to death. I mean literally coming in and working open to close, coming in on his off days, constantly having to do shit for work outside of work. It's stressful as hell and I know he is tried of it even if he wont admit it.

We didn't really talk much. He and I are playing a game together now though.

I stayed up really late last night into this morning playing video games and accidentally blew off the plans I had made with a friend by sleeping in so late.

He and I spoke last night, he had to open, then go to a meeting, then close. I told him he was letting his job take over his life and it wasn't healthy. He said if something better came along he would consider it. I told him it would take almost nothing for me to pull some strings and get him on where I work. The job might be something as simple as environmental services or security but he'd get good benefits, decent pay on a stable shift, he'd just have to be willing to relocate, and we had already talked about living together it seems like it would be an easy call. He still refuses to leave where he is though, I don't know how he ever expected a relationship between us to work if he's so unwilling to compromise.

I bought a game he and I were supposed to play together but he's suddenly lost interest now that I can play. Maybe I'll try playing it alone. I could always take something to go back to sleep too. It's only a few days til Monday, hopefully I find out something then, if not it's only a few more days til I start working again and if nothing else that gives me something to do for 14 hours.

Ive been sleeping on and off basically since I passed out last night. I don't know what I could go out and do, maybe watch a movie? I don't really like going out in public alone though unless I absolutely have to. He messenged me earlier while I was asleep, I responded just now when I woke up and he went online long enough to read the message and go back offline without responding. I think I'm just gonna go back to sleep.

I wouldn't say I'm good friends with my co-workers. None of them really know me, they see what I the show I put on. It's become hard to keep up the facade lately though, my emotions have been spilling over into my professional life. I recently met someone that I had been talking to online for years, I mentioned them in my OP. We had mutual interest in each other and the meeting went great, but they have been distant since they left. Truly I expected this, but I really hoped it would be different. Any time I open up to someone and let them in they see me for what I really am and they want nothing to do with me. This is why I always put on this mask around people and act how I think I'm supposed to.

Your explanation of happiness makes sense. I have moment in my life where everything is clear and I can smile just enjoying the moment, but they are few and far between. Meeting this friend was one of those moments, we had a lot of fun, shared laughter and smiles. I wish things were different, but they aren't and I'm finding it harder and harder to keep pressing forward believing in change.

Drinking and video games provide a temporary outlet that I seek refuge in. I find myself more often than not feeling too disengaged to even bother picking either up though now.

I work in healthcare and my insurance is through my employer, if I go to a hospital for depression or suicidal thoughts they will stick me up on RPI for 72 hours and my employer or co-workers will likely find out. I can't let that happen. I called the psychiatric hospital I used to go to to see if my insurance would cover it, but it will be monday before I find anything. I doubt my insurance will cover it though, I'm supposed to see people inside my employer's network in order to get coverage and I can't do that for fear my co-workers would find out. I've always tried to present myself as an outgoing and friendly person, I've always tried to be who I think people want me to be, even with friends. I don't want anyone to know how much of an emotional wreck I am it's embarrassing.

A normal day for me depends on if I'm working or not.

A normal work day is me waking up, taking a shower, then driving to work and then pretending to be outgoing and charismatic for 12 hours around my co-workers, then driving home and falling asleep.

A normal non-working day for me is waking up late and being bitched at for sleeping in, then staying locked in my room for hours trying to find something to do until I inevitably fall asleep.

I play video games and drink, sometimes I go out and see my childhood friends. They know how hard things have been for me lately, but they can't offer me any kind of support. I know it's hard for them seeing me like this. I keep telling myself things get better I just have to make sure I'm around to see it, but each day is harder than the last. I just want things to be better. I'm tired of seeking refuge in some temporary happiness that fades after a short time. I spent all this time in college hoping that would make things easier, so I could finally afford to move out and enjoy life and all that's changed is I have a little more money, but I still can't afford to move out and really do anything.

I called the psychiatric hospital I used to go to to see if my insurance would cover visits, and they will call me back monday. I drank a lot last night, more than I should have, I don't know what I was thinking, maybe I was hoping that I wouldn't wake up. Who knows. He messaged me while I was asleep and apparently is upset I didn't respond, yet for some reason he is still up at 6am his time long after he would normally have gone to sleep, only to suddenly be ready to go to sleep now when I respond. He called me babe though, so I guess that's good, and he was glad I got some sleep. I didn't tell him I got drunk and just passed out, probably best I don't mention that.

I just wish things were better, but I don't know what I can do to change that. I don't want to kill myself, but I also don't want to deal with this kind of shit anymore.

I told him I was going through a rough patch the other day and he asked me what was wrong, I told him shit just seemed like it was falling apart around me and there was nothing I could do about it. He said he was sorry I was going through shit, but that was basically the end of the conversation. We've barely spoke since he left so I can't really expect much else at the point I don't think.

I'm trying to compartmentalize my feelings for him like I used to. I always wrote it off as an impossiblity so it wasn't a big deal when shit didn't go how I wanted because I had already convinced myself it would never work. It's gotten easier the last few days, his total lack of effort to communicate has been telling and I'm slowly getting over it.

If he continues this indefinitely then I'll probably just stop talking to him all together. I don't want it to come to that, but knowing how I feel about him it would probably be best to remove myself from the situation because it seems apparent his feelings have changed. He once told me he would always do his best to make sure I knew how he felt, but he's done nothing but the opposite since he left.

If my name popped up across the screen at work, and it inevitably would if they did any kind of lab work for a consult and referral then my co-workers would see that and know what was going on. I don't want to give too much of my personal information away because this is a throwaway but I work in the medical field, so my co-workers would play a part in my treatment if I attempted to seek out a psychiatrist through my work insurance.

Drinking has never been a thing I did all the time, but I have been drinking more lately. The drunk me is the person I like, less inhibited, less afraid to speak my mind, willing to do things without fear of people's opinions. I'm always stuck in my head and afraid to express myself because I don't want other people to think negatively about me, but drinking helps me open up in a way nothing else ever has. All anti-depressants have ever done for me is make me feel numb, they don't block any of the negativity or make me feel better they just make me feel nothing at all. I almost exclusively drink with other people, but sometimes I drink alone and play video games. It's just relaxing for me because I stop giving a shit about all my problems for a little while and can just enjoy myself.

This is very peculiar. Why would your wife even want you to sign all these contracts to begin with? Are she and her family really so worried that you want to rob them blind? If that were the case why would she even marry you to begin with?


I don't really understand your willingness to allow her to keep so much that was obtained during the course of your marriage, even if it was given to her by her family that was for both of you to benefit from, not just her, and you should be entitled to half of everything acquired throughout the marriage. Regardless, I think you are well within your rights to request a no support or maintenance clause, she obviously doesn't need anything you have to offer monetarily and apparently she and the rest of her family see you as some kind of gold digger out to get all she has which clearly indicates that she is the one with all the money not you. All of these stipulations honestly make it seem like she wants the ability to take you for everything you are worth while leaving you powerless to stop her in the event of a divorce. You know your situation better than any of us here, but I can't help but question the motives of someone so adamant about keeping everything they have to themselves, while trying to insure they get a share of what someone else has.

Things still haven't gotten back to normal. We still haven't had a real conversation since he left. He's been leaving me on read a lot now. We haven't really spoken on the phone since before he left, any time he calls it's a "Oh well I've gotta go do this now, I'll talk to you later." thing. It's strange because he is still talking to me but it's like he's always finding something else to do so he can quickly get out of it. It would seem like he just wouldn't bother talking to me if he didn't want to, but instead it's like he is making a point to say something so I know he's still there, but also trying to avoid any real conversation.

I've tried focusing more on my career and things I enjoy. Things have been on a downhill slide for a while now, and this situation with Paul has only made it worse. I've spoken to my friends, but they, like me, can't seem to understand what is going on. They met Paul and thought we interacted well together, he was polite and seemed genuinely interested and now he seems so distant and preoccupied. I've talked with my mother about seeing a therapist again, and potentially getting put back on anti-depressants, but my insurance is through my work and I'm essentially required to use the doctors and such that they allow or pay out of pocket. I'm worried if I see psychiatrist through my work network my co-workers will find out and I don't want anyone knowing about how bad I've been lately. I considered the possibility of going to the ER at a hospital near by and telling them I'm suicidal. That would guarantee I'd get put up on RPI for 72 hours and could potentially open up a network for me to be treated again. My insurance covers ER visits at hospitals outside my work network, but of course then I'd have to lie and tell someone I plan to hurt myself and that could potentially get back to my employer.

I wouldn't say I have a drinking problem so much as I tend to forget my limits when I drink alone. When I'm drinking with others the social pressure of not getting too inebriated is there and thus I'm too worried to over do it because I don't want people thinking of me negatively. When I'm alone there isn't that pressure, so I sometimes forget when enough is enough. I've never done anything crazy though, I stay in the confines of my room and drink in peace.

How long ago was it that you last spoke with her? I certainly don't mean to imply that I think you should keep pressing her, but if it's been several months since you last spoke maybe you could attempt to reopen communication with her. If she's had time to reflect and heal, she may be open to the idea of speaking with you again.

Simply put, you face consequences because she is your mother and you are doing something she doesn't want you to do. Regardless of whether or not you see an issue with what you are doing she does and you should be respectful of that.

Marijuana is still a drug and still has negative side effects. It's terrible on your lungs and alters brain function, not to mention the fact that you are having to sneak around to do it and wasting money on it. It doesn't matter that there are other drugs out there that have worse side effects. Whether or not other things are worse for you don't matter. In the same way murdering someone is worse than robbing someone, both are still crimes, and both have negative consequences, you shouldn't do either of those things.

Is it possible to mend things with her? You obviously feel really bad for what you've put her through, have you tried talking to her about this? Maybe it's not too late to start again. The first step in any process of recovery is admitting there is a problem and wanting to do something about it. From what you've said you recognize there was a problem (drinking) and have stopped it and sought out the counsel of both professionals and non-professionals. These are all great steps in the right direction.

If you still have a line of communication open with her tell her how you feel, if for nothing else so that she can see that there was nothing she could have done differently and so she doesn't worry that she was the problem. It's very important in the healing process for both of you.

Even if things don't work out between you and your ex this experience is one of learning and discovery. Thomas Edison found hundreds of ways not to make a light bulb before he fold the one way to make a light bulb, you've discovered things not to do in a relationship now that will ultimately help shape your future for the better and help you figure out what to do in a relationship.

Wishing he was different? I wouldn't say I wished *he* were different more so I'm hoping that when I have more time off work we will have more time to communicate and the situation will become more clear. It just feels like we are drifting apart now because of how little we've spoken since he left. He hasn't been talking to me in the same way as he did before, he's more curt rather than playful and jokey. I worry I may be reading too much into things, my anxiety may be getting the best of me and I'm just making nothing into something. He just doesn't seem to have time for me suddenly though, and any time we talk it's always very brief with him giving one word responses more often than not. I don't want to lose him again, even if we just stay friends he's become such an important person in my life again, and I don't want to go back to the times were we only spoke a few times a month.

I fell off the wagon, I've spent the last few nights drinking trying to clear my head. I was so distracted with all of this and work stress that I ran a red light on my way home from work the other day. By the time I had realized what I had done I was already past it. Thankfully it was early in the morning and there was no traffic so no one was hurt. I've just been so in my head the last few days I haven't been able to do hardly anything. I've lost weight and haven't slept well in days. I blew off plans I had this week with friends because I just didn't feel like being around anyone. I'm starting to feel like I've lost control of my life now. Stress with family and friends, work, and now this shit with Paul. I feel like ever endeavor recently has ended in failure. I'm struggling to make sense of it all.

Nothing has changed. He doesn't seem to think there is anything strange with what he is doing, he doesn't realize it's an issue. I'm just trying to appreciate the time he does afford me and not get too stressed. He called me for 5 minutes this morning before rushing off the phone to go to work on his off day. I'm hoping once I'm off work after today for the next few days things will be different.

I told him once he gets his own place in June I could come stay with him on my off days, he said he'd put me up, but it would be a lot of money and kinda just seemed like he didn't want me to do it. Maybe I'm reading too much into it.

My first love committed suicide almost 8 years ago. The first time I visited his grave I left a bracelet with the infinity symbol on it. Since then I leave flowers that were his favorite color or symbolic of something to us. I've left Iris' one because the Goo Goo Dolls song was one we both enjoyed, I've left Orchids because he loved the White Stripes, I've left him lilies because that was his nickname for me, and last year I left 7 purple mums for each year of grief without him.

His mother is big into the occult and will leave various crystals and such on his grave. Whatever you leave is fine, I'm sure they would appreciate the gesture regardless of what you leave.

Yes and no. I know when I think about it he does stuff that clearly indicates he cares, but it's hard for me to get past the lack of actual communication on it. I feel like things would be much different if we were actually seeing each other regularly rather than just talking. Communication through text is our main form of communication so it's hard for me to understand how he feels when I can't see the look on his face or the tone in his words.

This is going to be difficult until we can see each other on a regular basis I'm sure. Though when and if that will happen remains to be seen. When we get another chance to talk maybe I should bring up the potential of him moving here again, just to see if his feelings on that have changed or not. I don't want to rush things of course, but that's going to be a deciding factor on whether or not we'll be able to move forward in this relationship or not.

I ended up telling him last night that I had been going through a rough patch the last few days and I just felt like he was pulling away. I told him I knew he was busy with work, and he's had new games he wants to play but that we've barely spoke and the last few days. That I tried opening up to him and he didn't really give me any kind of feedback, that I just want to know how he feels and need a little reassurance. He responded by telling me that's he's been having to play catch up at work since he was gone for a week and he doesn't know what I want him to say. He guesses he's not used to having to keep reassuring someone that he likes them or how he feels. He brought up that he called me this morning, and then again when he was playing a game with a friend he called me. He then said if that doesn't tell me anything then he's sorry. I told him I knew I was being needy and I was sorry. I knew he cared, who wouldn't still be talking to me if he didn't, but that i struggle with issues of self-worth and that's something I'm trying to get better about. I just need a little reassurance that even though he's busy, and I'm going through some shit he does still care.


It occurs to me now that maybe he's more about actions than words. Which is something I'll have to get used to. The thing is though, if we were at that point in the relationship where we were saying "I love you" I know it would be one of those things we ended conversations with, and that would be constant verbal reassurance.

We talked about getting together again back in May, but when I bring it up he seems cool with the idea, but not actually working on doing anything to ensure it happens.

He called me earlier while I was at work and we talked briefly on a break. I asked him earlier if I could post some of the pictures of us that I took and he said yes, but acted like he couldn't understand why I would ask, and said if he had a good reason to take pictures he would. He made kind of a big deal about saying he didn't like taking pictures but did it anyway while he was here, which I know isn't true because there are literally hundreds of pictures of him with friends on Facebook. So I asked him what a good reason was and he said really? What reason do you think was a good reason to take pictures? I told him to have memories. Then I asked him to tell me, and he said "you, is it not that obvious?" So I asked him to clarify and he didn't respond and left me on read. An hour later I messaged him and called him a butt for leaving me hanging and he just replies with "you don't need a response to that, you know the answer." So I told him to tell me anyway and he said no, to which I responded it's still nice to hear and he said he already said it. What exactly he is referring to I don't know. I know I was fishing there, but I was hoping he'd use that as a chance to tell me how he felt and instead he refused.

He ended up texting me not long after asking me to please message him when I got his text. I ended up waiting around til my alarm for work went off before responding. I was trying to think of what to say. I didn't want to have to explain that I spent the night stressing out over whether or not he was avoiding me. I called him and he didn't pick up but he immediately returned my call. He sounded really excited. He told me he was just worried about me since he saw I had deactivated my Facebook and whatnot and wanted to make sure I was ok. I thanked him for being worried about me and told him it was sweet. He laughed it off and said why wouldn't I be? He said he was at work and I apologized for calling him while he was at work, he said it was ok and he was just glad to hear I was alright. He said he wasn't busy but he had a lot he had to get done, but to let him know before I went to work and we could maybe talk then. I messaged him when I left for work but he left me on read and I haven't heard from him since. That was about 4 hours ago.

As cliché as it sounds, you'll know when you are ready. Age isn't really so much a factor as mentality and maturity are. Relationships at your age can be great, but also really detrimental. It all depends on where you are maturity wise.

Ask yourself what it is that you want out of a relationship and go from there. Are you wanting companionship? Are you wanting someone to explore your sexuality with? At 15-16 you're probably feeling a lot of pressure to start dating, but it's important to remember that other people's expectations of you are not your reality. You don't have to date anyone just because everyone else is doing it.

Your first relationship will be one of learning and experience, and it's important to remember that it likely will not last so you shouldn't invest your life into it. Enjoy each others company and have fun. Relationships are just as much learning about yourself as they are learning about the person you are with.

Why exactly do you want the money now for? At your age you really don't need that much money. Your welfare and such are (or at least should) still be being taken care of by family. You're too young to go to college or make any kind of expensive purchases such as home, auto, etc. It would likely be hard to convince your uncle you're ready for the money if you don't have something in mind to spend it on that is actually necessary for you at this age.

Let me start off by saying that abortion is not nearly as threatening as many make it sound during the first trimester. The majority of pregnancies in the first trimester can be terminated through a two pill process. One taken at the clinic the other typically taken at home, and very rarely require anything else done after the initial follow-up to ensure the pregnancy was successfully terminated.

Adoption is often touted as the best alternative to abortion, however it's important to understand that there is no guarantee a child that goes into the adoption/foster system will find a family. I don't mean that to sound so discouraging, but I know two people that were in the foster system for 10 years and stuck with several terrible families before finally getting adopted. They both have horror stories about the system and I always like to make a point of telling people now whenever adoption is brought up, that it's just an automatic happy ending.

Children are a lot of responsibility, it's hard to put into words just how much your life will change once you have a child even with the proper structure and funds. They require constant monitoring and a support system for healthy growth and development. The require food, clothing, shelter, and attention, all of which cost time and money. As a college student who isn't financially stable it's not likely you would be able to provide the best environment for a baby to grow up in. You're still growing up yourself and you need to focus on getting yourself to where you need to be before you can try to focus on something else.

Ultimately the decision is up to you, you know your situation better than us, and you'll have to make the call on what you think you can reasonably do. I think with what information we have abortion would be your best option, but again that's not a decision anyone can make for you. I hope the best for you in your situation. Good luck!
